channel.title: One Big Idea
channel.description: One idea. Under 60 seconds. Every day.

item.title: How to Change Your Life in 90 Days (Jay Shetty's Method)
item.description: How to change your life in 90 days without burning out: Jay Shetty's approach from his On Purpose podcast. Do less, pair hard tasks with something you enjoy (temptation bundling), and use if-then plans so habits stick. Explained and animated in our own words.

item.title: Why You're Still Tired After Resting All Weekend
item.description: On his podcast On Purpose, Jay Shetty suggests that if rest isn't restoring your energy, you may be resting from the wrong thing. Rest from whatever actually drained you, not just from work in general. Explained and animated in our own words.

item.title: Sharks Are Older Than Trees
item.description: The earliest shark-like scales in the fossil record date to about 450 million years ago, while the first trees appeared around 385 million years ago. For tens of millions of years, sharks swam in oceans next to land with no forests at all. Modern shark groups came much later, but the shark lineage beat trees by a long way.

item.title: Turn Your Phone Gray to Scroll Less
item.description: Cognitive neuroscientist Dr. Sahar Yousef suggests switching your phone to grayscale. Without bright colors, apps are less stimulating, which can make mindless scrolling easier to resist. Explained and animated in our own words.

item.title: NASA Lost a $125 Million Spacecraft Over Units
item.description: In 1999 NASA lost the Mars Climate Orbiter because one piece of ground software produced thruster data in imperial units (pound-force seconds) while the navigation software expected metric units (newton-seconds). The spacecraft flew too low and was lost.

item.title: The 5-Second Trick That Beats Procrastination
item.description: The 5 Second Rule, popularized by author and podcaster Mel Robbins: when you feel the urge to act on something you know you should do, count 5-4-3-2-1 and move before you talk yourself out of it. Explained and animated in our own words.
